items.title: 10 agent evals every AI engineer should know
items.summary:
10 agent evals every AI engineer should know

1) golden set

a frozen set of cases you run after every prompt model or tool change

use it as your baseline to see whether the system improved or quietly broke

OpenAI Evals helps you build repeatable benchmark sets and compare model changes

→ https://t.co/dr1GZlC75R

2) llm as judge

a second model scores open ended answers against a written rubric

use it when there is no exact output to compare against

OpenEvals provides ready made evaluators for LLM applications

→ https://t.co/S2yhnByFIP

3) rubric scoring

score correctness tone safety and cost separately

one quality number hides the problem

DeepEval helps you create custom metrics and score every dimension independently

→ https://t.co/q9Z6Xmixia

4) trajectory eval

grade the path the agent took

not only the final answer

AgentEvals checks agent actions decisions and tool calls across the full trajectory

→ https://t.co/0oziAl54az

5) tool unit tests

test every tool with fixed inputs and outputs

no model in the loop

MCP Inspector helps you inspect and test MCP servers tools and responses separately

→ https://t.co/IVmt5qpWIN

6) regression suite

replay previous runs against every new prompt model or toolset

then compare the results

Promptfoo helps you run repeatable eval suites catch regressions and add checks to CI

→ https://t.co/zxi2PuWuhe

7) a b in prod

split real traffic between two versions and compare actual outcomes

GrowthBook provides feature flags controlled experiments and product analytics

→ https://t.co/DGlE3JjDD3

8) human review

sample real runs and let a person grade them honestly

use it to calibrate your automated judge

Argilla helps teams collect human feedback review outputs and build better datasets

→ https://t.co/QHWb7skWjr

9) shadow run

let the candidate run on real traffic while its output is shown to nobody

use it before a risky rollout

Langfuse helps you trace production runs compare candidates and monitor eval results

→ https://t.co/IrhDf38tRn

10) red team

attack the system before somebody else does

jailbreaks prompt injection data leaks and tool abuse

Garak scans LLM systems for vulnerabilities and unsafe behavior

→ https://t.co/w8ObyW4ZKv

offline evals tell you it works

online evals tell you it still works

you probably do not need all ten today

start with the two that would have caught your last outage

items.title: Wind Financial Morning Post: July 29, 2026
items.summary:
Wind Financial Morning Post: July 29, 2026

Market Brief

Commerce Ministry: Reasonable and compliant industrial subsidy policies do not cause so-called "overcapacity"

AI trading faces "Black Tuesday": Chip stocks suffer heavy sell-off, KOSPI plunges nearly 11%

Fitch: AI market correction is becoming a major global credit risk

Mediators believe the U.S. and Iran are close to reviving the memorandum of understanding

The 2026 Fortune Global 500 ranking is released, with Amazon overtaking Walmart as the world's largest company

Apple launches new device leasing program in the U.S., market value surpasses $5 trillion for the first time

The wave of share buybacks and insider purchases in A-shares continues, with Zhongji Innolight planning to repurchase shares with a maximum outlay of 8 billion yuan.

Changxin Technology is included in the MSCI China All Shares Index, effective August 10

Top Stories

Global AI trading faces "Black Tuesday." South Korea's "memory giants," SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, both fell over 13%, dragging the KOSPI down nearly 11% to close, marking its largest single-day drop since March 4, with circuit breakers triggered again during trading. The Nikkei 225 plunged nearly 4%, Kioxia dropped over 18%, Tokyo Electron and Advantest fell over 10%. A-share and Hong Kong-listed semiconductor and AI computing stocks experienced deep corrections, with Demingli, GigaDevice, and others hitting daily trading limits; Xin Yisheng, Yuanjie Technology, and Zhongji Chuangchuang all declined over 15%. In the U.S., the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell more than 6% intraday, closing down over 4%. SanDisk slid more than 14%, SK Hynix dropped nearly 9%, Micron Technology and AMD both fell over 8%.

Mediators believe the U.S. and Iran are nearing a breakthrough agreement and may revive the memorandum of understanding signed in June. Oman has proposed a new joint management mechanism for the Strait of Hormuz, with users voluntarily contributing to a fund for maintaining the shipping lane, but the current negotiation outlook remains uncertain. Iran's military warned against accepting U.S. use of Iranian assets for "compensation," stating that Iranian vessels would otherwise be barred from passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Yemen's government warned that the Houthi movement might "emulate Iran" by controlling the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. However, the Houthis stated the Bab el-Mandeb Strait has not been closed, and recent announced blockade measures "target only Saudi Arabia."

The 2026 Fortune Global 500 ranking has been released. The total revenue of this year's listed companies reached approximately $43.1 trillion, exceeding one-third of global GDP and rising about 3.2 percent from last year. Amazon has become the world's largest company, ending Walmart's twelve-year reign at the top. Walmart ranks second, while China State Grid remains third. UnitedHealth Group and Saudi Aramco rank fourth and fifth, respectively.

The trend of share buybacks, insider purchases, and dividend distributions in A-shares continues to intensify. On the evening of July 28, more than 20 A-share companies announced plans for share repurchases, insider purchases, or interim dividends. Among them, Zhongji Innolight plans to repurchase shares with an investment of 4 billion to 8 billion yuan; Hailiang Holdings plans to increase its stake by 600 million to 1 billion yuan; BOE Technology's controlling shareholder plans to increase its holding by 500 million to 1 billion yuan. Additionally, seven companies including Huadian International, Capchem, Ningbo Port, and Haohua Energy have unveiled interim dividend plans.

China Macro & Policy

The Commerce Ministry, addressing the so-called "overcapacity" issue, stated that industrial subsidies are not inherently linked to overcapacity; reasonable and compliant industrial subsidy policies help correct market failures, promote technological innovation, protect the ecological environment, reduce poverty, and foster balanced development, and do not cause so-called "overcapacity." High export volumes and large trade surpluses do not equate to overcapacity; China has never deliberately pursued trade surpluses. The argument that "insufficient domestic demand in China leads to overcapacity" is inconsistent with reality.

The Ministry of Finance and the State Administration of Taxation announced that tax exemption benefits for major production and operational land used by enterprises in industries such as coal, mining, oil and gas, building materials, and power will be canceled. However, tax exemptions for land used for public welfare, security, and major infrastructure purposes within these industries will be retained.

In the first half of this year, China's tax revenue exceeded 10 trillion yuan, up 4.9% year-over-year. 126 million individuals benefited from personal income tax special additional deductions, with tax reductions exceeding 320 billion yuan. Tax cuts, fee reductions, and tax refunds supporting technological innovation and manufacturing development amounted to 1.91 trillion yuan. The number of overseas travelers processing tax refunds increased by 366% year-over-year.

China Equities Markets

The A-share market opened lower and continued to decline. The SSE Index closed down 1.16% at 3,813.31 points, the Shenzhen Component Index fell 4.52%, the ChiNext Index dropped 7.35%, the Star 50 Index slid 6.33%, and the Wind All China Index fell 2.7%. Market turnover reached 2.04 trillion yuan. On the board, PCB-related stocks continued to weaken, CPO themes plunged sharply, and storage chip concepts underwent deep corrections. Large consumer goods and banking stocks rose against the trend, while fiscal and tax digitalization and brain-computer interface concepts remained strong.

The Hong Kong market fluctuated upward. The Hang Seng Index closed up 0.41% at 25,310.85 points, the Hang Seng Tech Index rose 0.61%, and the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index increased 0.85%. Automotive and consumer stocks strengthened. Semiconductor, CPO, and large model stocks tumbled, with Zhipu and Jiankang Technology plunging nearly 19%, and GigaDevice falling over 17%. Southbound funds net sold nearly HK$2.5 billion.

Shenzhen Information, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, announced that it will launch the ChiNext Intelligent Driving Index on July 31. The index will select 50 stocks from ChiNext-listed companies engaged in intelligent driving-related fields including intelligent perception, decision-making algorithms, positioning and navigation, and intelligent automotive components, based on higher market capitalization.

QFII holdings are gradually being disclosed. As of July 28, 14 listed companies have disclosed QFII holdings, with a total market value of approximately 11.995 billion yuan. Among them, QFII held 27.3666 million shares of CATL and 19.4441 million shares of Jincheng Technology; holdings in Zhonglan Environmental Protection and Hainan Mining exceeded 7 million shares; holdings in Suzhi Testing and Zhengtai Power exceeded 4 million shares.

MSCI announced that Changxin Technology, due to its IPO, will be included in the MSCI China All Shares Index, effective August 10. Based on its latest total market capitalization, if successfully included, Changxin Technology could become the second-largest market cap constituent in the index, behind Tencent Holdings.

China Industry News

According to PBOC statistics, as of the end of the second quarter of 2026, the RMB real estate loan balance stood at 50.74 trillion yuan, down 4.9% year-over-year, with a reduction of 1.23 trillion yuan in the first half of the year. Among these, the real estate development loan balance was 12.65 trillion yuan, down 8.5% year-over-year, with a reduction of 540.2 billion yuan in the first half of the year. The personal housing loan balance was 36.29 trillion yuan, down 3.8% year-over-year, with a reduction of 716.3 billion yuan in the first half of the year.

China has launched a one-year special action to enhance the IPv6 capability of AI large models, aiming to strengthen large-scale application of IPv6 for large models, improve IPv6 management standards for large models, enhance IPv6 support levels for large model infrastructure, promote IPv6-driven traffic for large model applications, and advance the evolution of the internet toward native intelligence.

The 2026 China International Big Data Industry Expo will be held from August 28 to 30. The National Data Administration will release over 20 significant outcomes, including institutional norms, industry standards, and practice case collections. Leading enterprises and industry associations will also unveil over 40 new achievements in areas such as computing-power and electricity synergy, data circulation, and generative AI.

The "Self-Regulatory Convention for Token Cloud Services" has been officially released. The convention adheres to five core principles: legality and compliance, user-first, fair competition, open collaboration, and security-first. The initiators are committed to building a "safe, reliable, trustworthy, healthy, and standardized" token cloud service ecosystem and rejecting unfair competition.

Eleven departments jointly issued the "Action Plan for Strengthening Traditional Chinese Medicine in the Healthcare Foundation Project," proposing seven specific actions and 25 key tasks, including optimizing and improving the service network. The plan stipulates that by 2030, residents should be able to access TCM services within a 15-minute travel radius.

The China Banking Wealth Management Registration and Custody Center reported that as of the end of June this year, the total scale of China's bank wealth management market stood at 33.66 trillion yuan, an increase of 1.75 trillion yuan from the previous month. In the first half of the year, wealth management products generated a total income of 305.2 billion yuan for investors, with an average annualized yield of 2.05%.

Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Hangzhou held land auctions on the same day, with markedly differentiated market heat. A residential plot in Chaoyang's Jiuxianqiao in Beijing was sold for 4.6814 billion yuan after 248 rounds of intense bidding, with a premium of 25.8%. In Guangzhou's Liwan District, the highest premium reached 41%. Core urban plots in Shanghai achieved high-premium sales, while suburban plots were sold at base prices. In Hangzhou's Future Science City, two connected plots were sold at a premium but with cooling market enthusiasm compared to previous auctions.

Fintech

The U.S. government is accelerating the development of a regulatory framework for frontier AI models. Drafts were distributed two weeks ago to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and the three companies subsequently submitted revised comments. The framework requires AI giants to undergo a 30-day government review before publicly releasing their most advanced models.

Corporate News & Updates

On July 28, Apple Inc.'s market value briefly surpassed $5 trillion. Apple announced the launch of the "Apple Upgrade" program in the U.S., offering new product leasing services for iPhone, Apple Watch, Mac, and iPad, with iPhone leasing prices starting at $17.99 per month. Reports indicate Apple is nearing completion of the development of three new smart home products, including its first smart home hub device powered by a new Siri AI, as well as a new-generation Apple TV and HomePod mini.

Meta and BlackRock announced they will establish a joint venture to develop and operate a data center campus in El Paso, Texas, with a development cost of approximately $14 billion.

Amazon has made a major strategic adjustment to its AI strategy, downgrading several Nova flagship models to "maintain operations" status, ceasing further R&D investment. Some AI teams have been disbanded, and the company will concentrate engineering resources and computing power on developing next-generation frontier foundation models, shifting from multi-pronged deployment to focused breakthroughs.

Volcano Engine has launched DouBao Search, providing cross-language, multimodal, multi-domain online information queries. DouBao Search offers enterprises and developers 500 free searches per month; beyond that, pay-as-you-go pricing is available, or users can opt for monthly discounted packages to suit stable, large-scale usage needs.

BYD has confirmed that its humanoid robot product will be officially unveiled in August. BYD Executive Vice President Li Ke previously stated that the company plans to deploy humanoid robots in its dealer network for customer reception and product demonstrations.

Renault, a well-known automaker, faces criminal trial for suspected installation of exhaust emission cheating devices on diesel vehicles to evade environmental regulations. This is the second automaker, after Volkswagen, to be referred to a French criminal court over a "dieselgate" scandal. Volkswagen has already paid over 32 billion euros in fines.

U.S.-based Johnson & Johnson has reached a settlement agreement, agreeing to pay $5.5 billion to resolve approximately 69,000 lawsuits alleging its talcum powder products caused ovarian cancer. The proposed solution represents a potential "effective end" to litigation dating back to 2009.

Global Macro & Policy

The Federal Reserve is set to announce its latest interest rate decision. Market focus has shifted beyond whether rates will remain unchanged to the number of dissenting votes expected at this FOMC meeting. Multiple institutions and prediction markets believe two hawkish officials—Dallas Fed President Logan and Cleveland Fed President Harker—will cast dissenting votes at this meeting.

PJM, North America's largest grid operator, plans to implement new rules as early as mid-2027, whereby data centers failing to secure sufficient power in capacity market auctions will have their electricity temporarily cut during peak demand periods. This aims to prevent widespread blackouts and stabilize residential electricity prices.

Global Equity Markets

U.S. major indices closed mixed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.03% to 52,747.32 points; the S&P 500 increased 0.21% to 7,428.78 points; the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.22% to 24,876.91 points. IBM rose over 5%, leading the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The Wind US Magnificent Seven Index rose 0.69%, Google rose over 2%, and Microsoft rose over 1%. SpaceX rose over 2%. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index rose 1.08%, Autohome rose over 7%, and Luokong rose over 6%. The storage sector plunged, with SanDisk sliding more than 14%, SK Hynix falling nearly 9%, and Micron Technology and AMD both dropping over 8%.

European major indices closed higher. Germany's DAX rose 0.41% to 25,464.01 points; France's CAC 40 rose 0.63% to 8,458.78 points; UK's FTSE 100 rose 0.83% to 10,871.02 points. The temporary ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran led to a sharp drop in international oil prices, easing energy cost pressures and boosting market sentiment.

Asia-Pacific major indices closed lower. The KOSPI closed down 10.84% at 6,023.66 points, marking its largest single-day drop since March 4, having briefly fallen below the 6,000-point mark during trading; it has fallen nearly 29% since July. The Nikkei 225 closed down 3.95% at 62,364.92 points. India's SENSEX 30 fell 0.09% to 76,765.92 points.

South Korea's financial regulators are considering stricter position controls on individual stock leverage products, further tightening regulations beyond previously raised entry thresholds. The key proposal under study is to limit individual investment in stock leverage products to no more than 20% of their total financial investment portfolio.

Seagate Technology reported fourth-quarter revenue of $3.65 billion, up 48% year-over-year; analyst expectations were $3.49 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) were $5.71, exceeding analyst expectations of $5.08. Adjusted operating margin was 44.6%, compared to analyst expectations of 41.9%. The company forecast first-quarter revenue of $4 billion to $4.2 billion, above analyst expectations of $3.79 billion.

Coca-Cola reported second-quarter comparable revenue growth of approximately 6% to $13.37 billion, with adjusted earnings per share of $0.97, both exceeding market expectations. Coca-Cola slightly raised its full-year guidance, expecting full-year revenue growth of about 5% and earnings per share growth of 9% to 10%.

Corning reported second-quarter sales growth of 17% to $4.74 billion, with core earnings per share of $0.78, both surpassing market expectations. However, the company forecast third-quarter core sales of $4.9 billion to $5 billion, slightly below general market expectations.

Boeing reported second-quarter revenue of $24.6 billion, up 8% year-over-year; free cash flow reached $631 million, far exceeding market expectations. Core loss per share was $0.76, with a loss margin significantly wider than expected. Global backlog orders reached a record $715 billion.

Mercedes-Benz Group reported revenue of 63.663 billion euros for the first half of the year, down 4% year-over-year; net profit was 2.519 billion euros, down 6% year-over-year. The company lowered its full-year 2026 sales and revenue forecasts, expecting both to decline year-over-year, compared to prior expectations of roughly flat performance.

Bonds

The interbank bond market in China edged lower, with major government bond yields rising slightly, and treasury futures closed lower across the board. Liquidity tightened further, with the People's Bank of China conducting 305.5 billion yuan in reverse repurchase operations, net injecting 52.5 billion yuan. Traders noted that ahead of the Political Bureau meeting, the market lacked clear directional guidance, and short-term focus remains on liquidity changes and stock market performance.

International rating agency Fitch warned that the AI boom and its potential market correction are gradually becoming a major risk to global credit markets. As technology stock valuations soar and AI investment reaches record highs, while future earnings prospects remain highly uncertain, market concerns continue to intensify.

U.S. Treasury yields declined across the board. Commodities

U.S. crude oil futures fell 4.21% to $79.13 per barrel; Brent crude futures dropped 3.33% to $83.01 per barrel. The suspension of U.S.-Iran hostilities and ongoing dialogue have eased Middle East tensions, leading to a rapid retreat of the geopolitical risk premium that had previously pushed oil prices higher, significantly reducing concerns over supply disruptions and driving prices lower.

International precious metals futures generally fell. COMEX gold futures dropped 1.18% to $4,028.80 per ounce; COMEX silver futures declined 2.35% to $57.34 per ounce. Rising expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes, combined with elevated interest rate expectations suppressing precious metals, and the absence of substantive escalation in U.S.-Iran tensions, have fostered a cautious market sentiment, jointly contributing to the price weakness.
